messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Autoscaler observed sustained queue growth in gpu-pool-eu-west-1. Effective GPU capacity dropping. Symptoms: 5xx rate up, queue length > 2k for 12m. Pager sent to #incidents and infra-oncall.

devon: acked. oncall here. looking at autoscaler logs and driver metrics. initial thought: driver OOMs + node flaps reducing available GPUs.

sam: seeing lots of CUDA/Xid in driver logs (Xid 13/99). attaching tail from one node:```
[2026-03-15T10:12:01Z] nvml: Xid 13 on /dev/nvidia0
[2026-03-15T10:12:03Z] kernel: gpu0: fatal error, resetting
[2026-03-15T10:12:05Z] runtime: process oom-kill invoked for nvidia-driver
```

jin: autoscaler tried to add nodes but API rate limit hit on our cloud account twice, then hit pool cap (max nodes = 48). see: `autoscaler: scale_attempts=6, errors=[rate_limit, capacity_reached]`

alyssa: customers A and B report degraded responses. Support ticket 4129 shows timeouts / 504s. Notified account execs.

pete: on top of that, we've got several nodes in NotReady after kubelet restarts. node list excerpt:```
gpu-1001 NotReady 10m kernel-reset
gpu-1002 Ready 2m back online
gpu-1003 NotReady 8m oom-restart
gpu-1004 Ready 1m```

devon: mitigation plan: 1) pause recent driver rollout to prevent further regressions 2) open short-term manual scale to alternate pool (eu-west-spare-gpus) 3) throttle incoming traffic for affected routes via rate-limiter 4) escalate to runtime team for driver OOM signature analysis.

sam: paused driver rollout at 10:20 UTC. command used:```bash
sudo /opt/deployctl pause rollout driver-hotfix-2026-03-15
```

oncall-infra: manual scale request accepted. spinning up 12 nodes in eu-west-spare-gpus (expected ready ~4m). cloud ticket opened for rate limits (CID: CLD-8894).

alyssa: Implementing route-level throttling now. Reducing concurrency to 4 for /v1/generate for high-usage customers. This should shave peak by ~30%.

devon: quick health check after throttling + manual scale: queue length dropping from 2200 -> 950 in 7m, 5xxs down 45%. Not fully clear if driver restarts still causing capacity jitter.

jin: digging into driver logs across nodes, pattern shows OOM followed by nv-hostengine watchdog kicks:```
Mar 15 10:08:54 gpu-1003 kernel: Out of memory: Kill process 12345 (nvidia-driver) score 987 or sacrifice child
Mar 15 10:08:55 gpu-1003 kernel: Xid 46 detected, gpu reset initiated
Mar 15 10:09:00 gpu-1003 systemd: Started Nvidia driver crash handler
```

pete: hypothesis: a combination of larger sequence length requests + prefix caching misses caused memory pressure in driver on certain kernels (4.19.*). We rolled kernel->driver combo two nights ago.

devon: can runtime confirm whether this is new kernel-driver interaction? @jin @sam please advise.

sam: runtime looking at build matrix. The affected nodes are on driver 525.85 + kernel 4.19.12. We have a canary that showed increased memory usage under torch aten ops. Reproduced locally with config:```python
# repro script (simplified)
model = load_model('gpt-like', dtype='fp16')
for _ in range(200):
    out = model.generate(batch_size=32, seq_len=4096)
```
Triggers OOM on driver+kernel combo in ~3-5 loops.

alyssa: customer impact update: top three customers saw increased latency and ~10-15% request errors over last 20m. CS has sent templated update. No financial SLA breach yet but watching.

devon: action items now: - keep rollout paused - continue manual scaling to spare pool until autoscaler cap adjusted - runtime to produce hotfix or recommend driver rollback - infra to request temporary quota bump and unblock rate limits - ops to maintain throttling for 30m and monitor

jin: runtime will try two paths in parallel: 1) revert driver to 515.x (previous stable) on canary nodes 2) apply a memory-limit patch to driver malloc path and test in staging. ETA 45m for first results.

oncall-infra: cloud requested more justification for quota bump. I sent usage graphs + incident timeline. If approved, autoscaler will be allowed up to +20 nodes beyond pool cap for 1h.

pete: quick note: we should also flip autoscaler fallback to use smaller-VM GPUs (vm-type-gpu-sm) that are known stable. Devs, any objections?

sam: agree. Doing fallback config change now:```yaml
autoscaler:
  fallback_pools: [eu-west-sm-gpu, eu-west-spare-gpus]
  max_extra_nodes: 20
```
applied.

devon: paging summary for handoff: root cause under investigation (driver OOMs on kernel 4.19.12), current mitigations (paused rollout, manual scaling to spare pool, route throttling, autoscaler fallback to smaller GPUs), customer impact (elevated 5xx/latency, top customers notified), next steps (runtime hotfix or rollback, cloud quota request). Handoff to night oncall @pete for monitoring.

pete: taking over. I'll coordinate with runtime for rollback if we start seeing fresh OOMs after spare nodes come online. Please DM me any critical logs.

alyssa: leaving a note for post-incident: capture prompt patterns hitting long seq_len, add evals for driver combos, add alert for nvml Xid > 3 in 5m window.

devon: thanks team. I'll create a follow-up incident ticket with timeline + RCA owner assignment. Good job on fast mitigation. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident status: mitigated -> partial (traffic throttled, manual scale in place). Further escalation if new node OOMs detected.
